title: Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management: automatic preservation of deleted content for high-risk users
summary: The briefing's retention behaviour, controls and roadmap targets are supported. It correctly distinguishes the documented preview from the planned general availability release and reports the conflicting setup guidance rather than promising a default.

claims.claim: Roadmap item 392839 concerns automatic data preservation for high-risk users in Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview compliance portal: Data Lifecycle Management - Automatic data preservation for high-risk users

claims.claim: The roadmap plans automatic retention labels to preserve deleted emails and files based on a user's insider risk level.
claims.quote: The integration with Data Lifecycle Management will automatically apply retention labels to preserve deleted emails and files based on a user’s insider risk level.

claims.claim: Adaptive Protection moves users into and out of policies as their insider risk levels change.
claims.quote: automatically moving users in and out of policies as their risk levels change over time

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The automatic preservation integration targets users assigned the Elevated insider risk level.
claims.quote: retention labels are automatically applied to unlabeled content if it's deleted by users who have been identified as an elevated risk.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; Scope
claims.claim: Preservation covers content deleted from SharePoint, OneDrive and Exchange.
claims.quote: If these users delete content from SharePoint, OneDrive, or Exchange, a retention label is automatically applied to that content to retain it for 120 days.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The deleted content is retained for 120 days.
claims.quote: a retention label is automatically applied to that content to retain it for 120 days.

claims.claim: Learn documents application to unlabelled content, not content already carrying a retention label.
claims.quote: When you enable Adaptive Protection for your tenant, retention labels are automatically applied to unlabeled content

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Users do not see the automatically applied retention label.
claims.quote: Unlike other labeling scenarios, users don't see the retention label

claims.claim: After 120 days the retained items become eligible for permanent deletion.
claims.quote: After the 120 days expire, the items then become eligible for permanent deletion.

claims.quote: At this time, you can't change the retention period or assign different policies based on the different risk levels, or for different locations.

claims.claim: Different preservation policies cannot currently be assigned for different locations.
claims.quote: At this time, you can't change the retention period or assign different policies based on the different risk levels, or for different locations.

claims.quote: In preview, you can use this solution with Insider Risk Management so that retention labels are automatically applied with Adaptive Protection.

claims.quote: As a result, that content remains accessible for search and eDiscovery from the secured locations used by the workload.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The general availability default is not stated, so defaultState is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: Adaptive protection Data lifecycle management default general availability meter. Read roadmap, retention and Adaptive Protection articles: preview setup is documented with conflicting opt-in guidance, but no GA arrival default is stated.

claims.claim: The quick setup guidance says the policy is automatically created and applied when a tenant first turns on Adaptive Protection.
claims.quote: If you haven't already turned on Adaptive Protection, the policy is automatically created and applied when you turn on Adaptive Protection.

claims.claim: The custom setup note instead says explicitly opting in is necessary after turning on Adaptive Protection.
claims.quote: If you turn on Adaptive Protection for your organization, you need to explicitly opt in to apply the data lifecycle management policy.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Tenants that enabled and configured Adaptive Protection before this integration released must opt in to create the auto-labeling policy.
claims.quote: If you enabled and configured Adaptive Protection before this integration with data lifecycle management released, you'll need to opt-in to create this auto-labeling policy.

claims.claim: Insider Risk Management assigns insider risk levels using the activity and insights evaluated by the selected policies.
claims.quote: Depending on the Insider Risk Management policy assigned in Adaptive Protection, different criteria (users, groups, indicators, thresholds, etc.) are used to determine applicable insider risk levels.

claims.claim: Retention labels are applied automatically rather than requiring approval of each deletion.
claims.quote: If these users delete content from SharePoint, OneDrive, or Exchange, a retention label is automatically applied to that content to retain it for 120 days.

claims.claim: The integration uses a single retention label for the tenant.
claims.quote: The single retention label and auto-labeling retention policy for your tenant aren't visible in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: The integration uses a single auto-labeling retention policy for the tenant.
claims.quote: The single retention label and auto-labeling retention policy for your tenant aren't visible in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: The automatically created label and policy are not visible in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: The single retention label and auto-labeling retention policy for your tenant aren't visible in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Administrators do not have to create or manage the underlying retention label or auto-labeling policy.
claims.quote: you don't need to create or manage the retention label or auto-labeling retention policy.

claims.claim: Turning off the integration removes labels it applied, allowing the items to become eligible for permanent deletion.
claims.quote: Any retention labels that were applied as a result of Adaptive Protection are removed so that the items can then become eligible for permanent deletion.

claims.claim: The integration can be turned off without affecting other Adaptive Protection policies.
claims.quote: you can turn off the auto-labeling policy without affecting other Adaptive Protection policies.

claims.claim: The Data Lifecycle Management setting cannot be turned on unless Adaptive Protection is on for the tenant.
claims.quote: You won't be able to turn on this setting unless Adaptive Protection is turned on for your tenant.

claims.quote: | Configure Adaptive Protection and update settings | *Insider Risk Management* or *Insider Risk Management Admins* |

claims.claim: Turning off tenant-wide Adaptive Protection stops sharing insider risk levels with Data Lifecycle Management.
claims.quote: the system stops assigning insider risk levels to users and stops sharing them with data loss prevention, data lifecycle management, and Conditional Access.
